about.title: Azusa Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision upends everything, and Azusa families are often left facing funeral bills and lost income while still grieving. Los Angeles County recorded one traffic death alongside hundreds of injury crashes in the most recent reporting year, a reminder that corridors like the I-210, Azusa Avenue, Arrow Highway, and San Gabriel Avenue carry heavy, ongoing traffic. California law gives a limited group of survivors — typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and in some cases other dependents — the right to bring a wrongful death claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that connects grieving families in Azusa with an independent personal injury attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and next steps. You focus on your family. We handle the introduction, and any attorney you work with is paid only if there's a recovery.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing mainly to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain circumstances. An attorney can help sort out who qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Watching the Clock
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file, but claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Acting early preserves evidence and protects your family's options.

items.title: Recognizing What Can Be Recovered
items.desc: Losses in a wrongful death claim can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your family has lost, and the loss of companionship and guidance. An independent attorney can walk through how these apply to your situation.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Azusa?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That window shrinks significantly if a government entity, such as a public road agency, may be involved. Because Azusa's corridors like I-210 and Arrow Highway involve public infrastructure, it's worth checking this timeline early.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the at-fault driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate proceedings. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action your family can pursue for financial and emotional losses. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect us with an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service and not a law firm itself. We simply connect families with an independent attorney, who typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is obtained.
